description:
## Al-Haqqah - The Inevitable

(Revealed at Mecca)

52 Verses in 2 Sections

## Sections Of Surah Al-Haqqah

1. The Inevitable.
2. The Prophet and the Qur'an Testified.

## Important Topics

1. Disobedience to the Apostle of God brings God's chastisement - (Verse 9)
2. A single blast will remove away the mountains crushing them to nothing - (Verses 13, 14)
3. The happening of the Day of the Final Judgment - (Verses 15-37)
4. The allegations against the Qur'an, refuted - (Verses 38-43)
5.

## Al-Haqqah Section 1 - The Inevitable

The coming of the Inevitable Day of Judgment described

In the name of God the Beneficent the Merciful

## Al-Haqqah Section 2 - The Prophet And The Qur'an Testified

Testified that the Prophet is one, the most honoured with God, and not any poet and the Qur'an is a Reminder for the Pious ones.

25.1: See <{["Q", "84:10"]}>. For further details about right and left used in Qur'an in the group of the people see Verse <{["Q", "56:8"]}> till <{["Q", "56:47"]}>.

translations.1: The Reality (That which is sure to come) !
translations.3: And what did thou (O' Man) comprehend what the Reality is?
translations.4: Belied Thamood and 'Ad' the striking (Horrible) calamity (Resurrection. Refer to Verses <{["Q", "7:73"]}>-<{["Q", "7:78"]}>, <{["Q", "11:61"]}>, <{["Q", "51:44"]}>.)
translations.5: So as to Thamood, they were destroyed by an exceedingly terrible thunder
translations.6: And as to 'Ad, they were destroyed by a roaring violent blast
translations.7: He made it rage against them for seven nights and eight days uprooting, that thou mightest see the people therein prostrate as if they were the trunks of the hollow palms
translations.8: Seest thou then, of them any surviving?
translations.9: And came Pharaoh and those before him and the cities over-thrown, with evil
translations.10: And they disobeyed the Apostle of their Lord, so He seized (Gripped) them with an increasing seizure (Vehement – intense. Refer to Verse <{["Q", "11:42"]}>.)
translations.11: Verily, We, when rose the water (of Noah's flood) surpassed the (ordinary) limits, bore you up (O' mankind) in the Ark made to float
translations.12: That We may make it unto you a Reminder, and that retaining ears might retain it
translations.13: And when is blown by the Trumpet (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "6:73"]}>.) , a single blast
translations.14: And the earth and the mountains shall be borne away and crushed with a single crushing (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "89:21"]}>, <{["Q", "56:1"]}>-<{["Q", "56:6"]}>, Chapter – 101.)
translations.15: On that Day shall come to pass the Great Event (of Reckoning) (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "89:21"]}>, <{["Q", "59:1"]}>-<{["Q", "59:6"]}>, Chap. 101, <{["Q", "56:1"]}>.)
translations.16: And shall cleave asunder the heaven (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "84:1"]}>-<{["Q", "84:5"]}>.) , so that on that Day it shall be (mere) frail (Nebular State.)
translations.17: And the angels shall be on the sides of it; and above them shall bear that Day 'Arsh' (the Throne of Authority) of thy Lord, eight (The divine attributes of God.) (of them)
translations.18: On the Day ye shall be exposed, (and) shall remain not hidden any secret of yours
translations.19: Then he, who is given the (Record) Book (of his deeds) in his right hand (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "17:71"]}>, <{["Q", "84:7"]}>.) , will say: 'Lo! read ye my book! (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "35:11"]}>-<{["Q", "35:14"]}>.) '
translations.20: Verily, I did feel (Think – realise.) that I shall meet my account (See Verse <{["Q", "2:46"]}>.)
translations.21: So shall he be in a life (of bliss), pleased (with it)
translations.23: The fruits of it being low and near at hand
translations.24: (It will be said unto them): "Eat ye and drink ye for health and pleasure, for what goodness ye sent before (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "77:20"]}>.) you, in the days past (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:110"]}>.) !"
translations.25: But he, who is given the (Record) Book (of deeds) in his left (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "84:10"]}>-<{["Q", "84:12"]}>.) hand, will say: "O' that the Book had not been given me! (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "35:11"]}>-<{["Q", "35:14"]}>.)"
translations.26: And I had not known what my account was
translations.27: O' would that it had made an end (of me)!
translations.29: And hath gone from me (all) my power!
translations.30: (It will he said unto him)'. "Seize him ye (angels)" and fetter him!
translations.31: Then into the blazing fire burn him!
translations.32: Then into a chain, of the length of cubits, tie him into!
translations.33: Verily he used not to believe in God, the Great!
translations.34: And he urged not the feeding of the poor
translations.35: So for him here today there is not a friend
translations.36: And no food is for him save the refuse of the wash of wounds!
translations.37: Which shall eat none but the sinners!
translations.38: So, I swear (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "56:75"]}>, <{["Q", "90:1"]}>.) by what ye see!
translations.39: And what ye see (All-Enveloping - nothing left over.) not!
translations.40: Verily, it is the word of the most honoured Apostle!
translations.41: And it is not the word of a poet; (How) little it is what ye believe?
translations.42: Nor the word of a soothsayer; (How) little it is what ye reflect?
translations.43: It is a despatch descended from the Lord of the worlds
translations.44: And if (Our Apostle Muhammad) had fabricated against Us any of the sayings
translations.45: Certainly, would We have seized him by the right hand
translations.46: Then certainly would We have cut off his aorta
translations.47: And of you not one could have withheld (Us) against him
translations.48: And verily, it is a reminder unto the pious (Those who guard themselves against evil) ones. (Refer to Verse <{["Q", "2:142"]}> for the part of the Verse related to the Holy Qur'an as a source of guidance, and to <{["Q", "3:137"]}> for the part of the Verse related to the Holy Qur'an as a reminder.)
translations.49: And verily know We that some of you are the beliers
translations.50: And verily it is a great grief unto the disbelievers
translations.51: And verily, it is the very Truth, fully assured (Refer to Verses <{["Q", "102:5"]}>, <{["Q", "102:7"]}>.)
translations.52: So Hallow by the name of thy Lord, The Great!

exegesis.1:
The Inevitable: - That which shall surely come to pass without fail - when all falsehood shall vanish, only the absolute truth shall be laid bare - The word '_Alhaqa'_ is derived from '_Haq'_ or '_Haqiqah'_, i.e., the truth.

That which is sure to come - the inevitable, i.e., The Resurrection. (A.P.)
exegesis.2: The Resurrection, i.e., passing into new life or the coming into life after death, everyone individually and collectively, according to Qur'an is such a reality and so certain to happen that in many places has been termed as '_Haqq al-Yaqin'_ - the Certain Truth, as otherwise Qur'an considers the creation as meaningless. (A.P.)
exegesis.4:
'_Qariyah'_ derived from '_Qar'_ i.e., striking of one thing over the other - here meaning calamity striking terror by the events causing horror and awe in the hearts of the people - The Day of Doom which the people '_Ad'_ and '_Thamood'_ disbelieved and called it to be a lie. Qariah is another name for the terrible day of the Final Judgment<{["F", 1]}>.

Thamood, the people who defied the apostle '_Saleh'_ who hamstrung the 'She-Camel' which appeared by God's command - A Mighty Calamity consisting of earthquake and a terrible Thunderstorm overtook them and they were destroyed<{["F", 2]}>.
exegesis.6: '_Ad'_ the people who defied the apostle Hud, who were destroyed by a terrible violent blast of the wind<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.8: Not one left alive - Even those who took shelter under the underground cells, were blown out and killed.
exegesis.9:
Pharaoh whose inordinate pride and being puffed up with power, has passed into a proverb. He defied the apostle Moses and was destroyed<{["F", 1]}>.

The cities overthrown are Sodom and Gomorrah which defied the preachings of the apostle Lot - They were overturned<{["F", 2]}>.
exegesis.11: Reference is to the rescue that Noah along with his sincere followers being saved by through Ark<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.12:
According to the _Holyat al-aulia_, and Kashshaf Ms., etc. This Verse was revealed about Ali Ibn Abu Talib. The above authorities report that the Holy Prophet said: "_O' Ali! God hath commanded me, to always keep thee near me and not away from me - and I prayed to God to make thy ear such that whatever thou hearest of the Word of God and receiveth the knowledge from me, thou forgetteth not but preserve it always. I have been commanded by God to convey to you whatever knowledge I receive from Him"_ It was based on the strength of this divine gift that Ali on the day of his departure from this world, though mortally wounded in the head, by a strongly poisoned sword and the whole body having been affected by it, said "_Ask me whatever ye want to know, ere ye lose me!_" (MS. and others). This was one of the unique distinctions which Ali was blessed with, and it was for this position of Ali that after the Holy Prophet, everyone resorted to Ali for the solution of their problems, even Omar openly declared "_Had not Ali been there, Omar would have perished_"

A reminder for the common people who are forgetful and is a reservation in the minds of those who retain and reserve the guidance they receive from God, without their memory being interrupted. This is true of those persons who in the course of their development and progress towards God, have never been diverted from it, by the devilish and temporal forces. The Holy Prophet pointing it to Ali as the true example of the retaining ears confirm this. (A.P.)
exegesis.13: This refers to the inevitable event, the day of the Final Judgment. The whole creation will first pass through the destruction, to be raised once again to account for each one's faith and conduct. For the first blast<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.14: The whole physical world will pass away and a new one will be brought into being<{["F", 1]}>. The mountains which stand on the earth since its creation, with their hardness, will be rendered into powder and blown into the atmosphere. For what will happen on that day, to the earth and the mountains<{["F", 2]}>.
exegesis.17: The '_Arsh'_ i.e., the seat of the Might, Wisdom and Authority of God, will be borne by eight angels. Angels representing the various aspects of the divine attributes of God.
exegesis.19:
The righteous are called the Companions of the Right Hand<{["F", 1]}>.

Righteous are said to receive the record of their deeds in their Right Hand<{["F", 2]}>.
exegesis.23: There will not be the least difficulty or hindrance in the enjoyment of the bounties in the heaven. Fruits in bunches will be hanging low within the reach of everyone. All the descriptions of the heavenly bliss, given in the Qur'an, are figurative.
exegesis.24:
Everybody will be justly repaid for his deeds in this life<{["F", 1]}>.

The days gone by are referred to the life in this world for then the world be wholly new. This earth and the heaven would have been changed<{["F", 2]}>. There would not be the present conception or the realisation of even the time and the space.

The address 'Eat and drink' will be particularly to those righteous ones, who in this life, in the way of the Lord, suffered hunger and thirst and fasted to please the Lord.
exegesis.25:
In contrast to the righteous ones, the wicked ones, will be given the records of their deeds in their left hand who would remember their past life with agony and repentance which would be of no avail to them causing them a mental torture. They would like to have not been given any records at all<{["F", 1]}>.

Right always means the direction towards God and the left, i.e., to the material world. In this sense it is correct to term the direction 'left' as 'Backward'. (A.P.)
exegesis.27:
They would wish death to have been an end of the world and their life in it, but to their disappointment death was only a transition to a new world, in a new state of reality and actual realization.

This has always been the tendency of the evil doers when they face the consequence of their own misdeeds, they wished that they had not been in the know of it. (A.P.)
exegesis.29: Every soul would have lost hold on itself and the power and authority, as a whole, would be only of God and none else. He would be the only King, the Master, the Lord of the Day<{["F", 1]}>.
exegesis.32:
'Seventy Cubits' represent the enormity of the size and the weight and grievous nature of it.

Qur'an has a special reference to the number seven and its multiples, particularly in reference to the several stages or the aspects of hell as it is said. The justification for that is the five external and two internal senses through which the devilish temptations are affected<{["F", 1]}>. (A.P.)
exegesis.34:
The expression includes obstructing or preventing the dispensation of the poor-rate '_Zakat'_ and '_Khums'_ and the aims to the poor.

Not felt as necessary - Indicates the sympathy of the needy and service to them here, is of no avail in the hereafter. (A.P.)
exegesis.38: Falsehood always yields and gets vanished, giving place to Truth. Though one might deny God or call His word a lie or doubt the Truth and term it as poetry or folklore, but the nature, even that which is seen by man, the visible world itself is quite sufficient to prove the truth and establish it. This refers to the Holy Qur'an being the Word of God and not the fabrication of the Holy Prophet.
exegesis.40: The Holy Qur'an is the utterance of the Word of God by the Holy Prophet, who is God's Honoured one.
exegesis.44: This divine undertaking is to assert that those who have been commissioned by God, cannot but deliver whatever they are charged with, and God never allows them to forge anything of their own on His behalf. It does not mean that the imposters or the false prophets who forge lies and falsely claim to have been commissioned by God, need not be exposed - in this manner, the lack of evidence is itself sufficient to expose them. (A.P.)
